articles.title: Read a TLS certificate expiry check without turning every failure into expired
articles.excerpt: A certificate monitor that reports “expired” whenever a command fails will eventually send you on the wrong investigation. A missing file, a TLS handshake failure and a certificate approaching its exp…
articles.body: A certificate monitor that reports “expired” whenever a command fails will eventually send you on the wrong investigation. A missing file, a TLS handshake failure and a certificate approaching its expiry are different observations. Start with a file you already know represents the certificate you intend to monitor. Later, add a separate acquisition step for the live endpoint. Keeping those steps distinct makes failures explainable. Check the file before checking the threshold openssl x509 -in server.pem -noout -dates -ext subjectAltName openssl x509 -in server.pem -noout -checkend 604800 604800 is seven days in seconds. The -checkend option checks whether the certificate expires within that interval and uses a nonzero exit status when it will.

articles.title: Airlock: a veto window for your POT, built on Portaldot's Proxy pallet
articles.excerpt: A leaked hot key should not empty a wallet in one block. A multisig fixes that, but it needs a second signer for every payment, which is heavy for one person. The Portaldot runtime already has a bette…
articles.body: A leaked hot key should not empty a wallet in one block. A multisig fixes that, but it needs a second signer for every payment, which is heavy for one person. The Portaldot runtime already has a better primitive. The Proxy pallet can make a delegate announce a call, wait a set number of blocks, and only then execute it. Another delegate can reject the announcement in between. In my search (not a market survey) I did not find a product built around it, so I built one for the Portaldot Hacker House 2026. How it works airlock create makes a keyless vault ( proxy.create_pure ) controlled by two keys: Hot key , your daily key, registered with a delay (10 blocks = 60 s in the demo). It cannot move funds directly: the chain answers Proxy.Unannounced . It can only announce a call hash and wait.

articles.title: Ballast: freezing a test dollar on Portaldot when its reserve runs short
articles.excerpt: A custodial wrapped token fails silently: reserves leave, the token keeps moving, and holders learn last. Ballast is a safety layer for the first dollar on Portaldot. It is built around a clearly labe…
articles.body: A custodial wrapped token fails silently: reserves leave, the token keeps moving, and holders learn last. Ballast is a safety layer for the first dollar on Portaldot. It is built around a clearly labelled test asset, pUSDC-test , whose roles are enforced by the Portaldot V3 runtime itself (the native Assets pallet plus Multisig), with the reserve held in a ReserveVault contract on Ethereum Sepolia. One flow, four guarantees Mint needs a 2-of-2 multisig whose mandatory co-signer, the reserve bot, signs only if finalized reserves cover supply plus the amount. Reserves are attested on chain : BALLAST/1 remarks, mirrored into a ReserveOracle contract on Revive. ballast verify re-checks both chains and rejects a forged remark. A watcher set (a 1-of-2 multisig) can only freeze .

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 31, 2015: Creepy skull-shaped Halloween asteroid flies by Earth, NASA names it the 'Great Pumpkin'
articles.excerpt: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. Here's why it was so creepy.
articles.body: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. It arrived with excellent timing on Halloween, which made the already-creepy asteroid even creepier. During its closest approach, the creepy asteroid was about 300,000 miles from Earth, or 1.3 times the average distance between Earth and the moon . So, it didn't pose a threat to our planet. It was discovered by astronomers at Hawaii's Pan-STARRS observatory only three weeks before the flyby, and it was given the official designation "2015 TB145." But no one knew what it looked like until the day before Halloween, when the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico captured the first radar images.

articles.title: The moon, Mars, and Jupiter shine in the heart of the Lion overnight on Nov. 1-2
articles.excerpt: The waning moon shines with Jupiter, Mars and the brilliant star Regulus in the eastern sky overnight Nov. 1-2.
articles.body: The moon dives towards the glowing heart of the constellation Leo for a spectacular rendezvous with Mars and Jupiter overnight on Nov. 1-2, as the glittering stars of the Beehive Cluster shine nearby. Here's what you need to know. Look to the eastern horizon an hour after midnight to see the 45%-lit waning moon shining less than 5 degrees from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length to the night sky. Jupiter's bright light will gleam just below the red planet, with the bright star Regulus lining up beyond to form a dazzling procession leading back to the horizon. The stars of the Beehive Cluster (M44) can be found twinkling 10 degrees from the unlit side of the lunar disk around this time, in the middle of the constellation Cancer .

articles.body: The year was 2014. The live-action Disney remake craze had already begun thanks to the success of Tim Burton's Alice in Wonderland , but it hadn’t reached its box office peak. Meanwhile, on the other side of Hollywood, Sofia Coppola was attached to a movie bursting at the seams with possibilities: a live-action The Little Mermaid, not based on the 1998 Disney animated classic, but on the original Hans Christian Andersen fairy tale, where (spoiler alert) the brokenhearted mermaid dies by flinging herself into the ocean and dissolving into sea foam. I can picture Coppola’s compositions clearly in my mind: the mermaid (Elle Fanning) shot in pastel colors, thoughtfully looking out at the horizon. A song by The Strokes or Phoenix plays in the background.

articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 31 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Night on a Spooky Planet Explanation: What spooky planet is this? Planet Earth on a dark and stormy night, of course. The ghostly scene was photographed at Hverir , a geothermally active area found along northeastern Iceland’s volcanic landscape . Triggered by solar activity , geomagnetic storms have unleashed energetic particles trapped in Earth’s magnetic field.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
articles.author: Dan Goodin
